treatment.name: Wisdom Tooth Extraction
treatment.overview: Removal of impacted or problematic third molars to prevent pain, infection, and crowding.

types.name: Simple Extraction
description: For erupted wisdom teeth with sufficient access.

types.name: Surgical Extraction
description: Flap elevation and sectioning when needed.

cost.note: Varies with impaction depth, root anatomy, and need for surgical flap.

before: Medical history and consent; post-op instructions explained.
during: Stitches may be placed; gauze pressure for hemostasis.
after: Swelling peaks at 48-72 hours; use cold compress first 24 hours.
Sutures removed in 5-7 days if non-resorbable; follow-up review.

avoid: Straws and spitting (48 hours) to prevent dry socket
Hard/spicy foods; smoking/alcohol in early healing
prefer: Cold, soft foods (curd, smoothies, khichdi, soups)
foodGuidelines.tip: Start warm saline rinses after 24 hours; follow medication schedule strictly.

pros: No surgery or downtime if asymptomatic
cons: Decay in adjacent molars due to food trapping
Cyst formation or crowding (in select cases)
prosConsOfSkipping.summary: Timely removal prevents recurrent infections and protects neighboring teeth.

faq.a: The area is numbed; you’ll feel pressure but not pain. Post-op soreness is managed with medications.
Most patients resume routine in 1–3 days; complete healing takes a couple of weeks.
